headline: Taiwan shares close up 0.3% at 47,111.26 Friday after Thursday's 3.41% drop
summary: The Taiex gained 141.39 points on turnover of NT$935.96 billion. TSMC's Taipei shares slipped 0.8% on the first full session after its results.

headline: Reuters: CoreWeave 2031 bonds yield 15.78%; Oracle, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta CDS at records
summary: CoreWeave carries more than $50B of debt. Oracle, Nvidia and other big-tech credit default swaps rose this week; Amazon, Alphabet and Meta hit records but moved far less than CoreWeave or Oracle. Deutsche Bank's Jim Reid said AI financing costs show worrying signs at the edges.

headline: KOSPI +2.05% after Black Thursday; Samsung +2.6%, SK hynix +0.8%; Nikkei +1.4%
summary: Foreigners bought a net 172.1B won, ending an eight-session selling streak, after selling more than 3.6T won on Thursday. SK hynix faded from about +2.9% intraday. KOSPI is still 19.2% below its Oct 2 close; analysts called the buying a pause, not a reversal.

headline: Warsh gives no October signal in Bangkok: 'will make judgements at the October and December meeting'
summary: In his last appearance before the blackout, the Fed Chair said he does not pre-judge meetings and called the investment surge the main upside for the global economy. The dollar index slipped 0.2%.

headline: Asia rebounds after the chip rout: Nikkei +1.9%, Hang Seng +1.2%; Jakarta falls over 10% on MSCI warning
summary: After Thursday's US close (Dow +1.1%, S&P +0.3%, Nasdaq +0.1%), the Nikkei rose 1.9%, Hang Seng 1.2%, Shanghai 1% and the ASX 200 1.1%. Indonesia slumped on an MSCI downgrade warning; Brent eased 0.4% to about $105.5 (AP).

headline: TSMC raises 2026 sales growth forecast to about 44% in US dollars, keeps capex at $60-64B
summary: Up from slightly over 40% in July. CFO Wendell Huang kept 2026 capex at $60-64 billion and said 2026-2028 spending will exceed the prior three years. 2nm was 8% of Q3 sales, up from 3% in Q2. CoWoS remains customers' top choice and TSMC will add capacity to meet demand.

headline: TSMC call: AI accelerator growth 'probably will be higher' than mid-to-high 50s%; 'prudent' on 2027
summary: Management did not formally lift the 2024-2029 AI accelerator CAGR but said it will probably be higher. Consumer and price-sensitive segments are being challenged by rising component prices. Overseas-fab margin dilution to widen to 3-4 points later in the five-year period. N2 capacity to more than double in 2027; A14 risk production 2027.

headline: TSMC weighing Texas production and cooperation with Musk's Terafab; Arizona second fab in Q3 2027
summary: C.C. Wei said talks are at the discussion stage and TSMC would need to run any fab it works on. He said US expansion is driven by requests from major American customers. Arizona's second fab is slated for volume production in Q3 2027.

headline: Huang says CoreWeave needs no backstop as its credit swaps hit a record 1,194.5bp
summary: Speaking in Stockholm, Huang said CoreWeave's cost of capital is decreasing. The CDS level implies over 60% default odds within five years. Nvidia owns about 10% of CoreWeave. Separately reported, unconfirmed: talks to backstop $250 billion of OpenAI data-centre financing.

headline: Nvidia and Volvo Cars expand partnership on automated driving safety
summary: One of two Nvidia partnership releases Thursday; the other expands work with Adobe on agentic creation tools.

headline: Meta launches Muse Spark Open, an 816B-parameter open-weight model that runs on Mac Studio
summary: Natively multimodal with a 1 million-token context window, aimed at coding and agentic work; Meta calls it the most capable US open-weight model. Built with Apple to run locally; needs about 1TB of RAM. Available now through several API platforms.

headline: Tim Cook: Apple Intelligence with Alibaba's Qwen approved in China; beta due later in October
summary: Speaking in Shanghai, Cook said the first batch of core features can now be rolled out gradually: live translation, writing tools and photo cleanup. The upgraded Siri is not included.

headline: Anthropic gives six METR researchers employee-level access to assess its models and safety work
summary: METR gets company laptops and internal tools and will publish its own assessments; Anthropic can require redactions only in pre-set categories such as customer data. No IPO, S-1 or revenue update came with it.

headline: US PPI jumps 1.3% in September, most in 4-1/2 years; retail sales +0.8% but core sales only +0.1%
summary: Producer prices rose 1.3% (0.5% expected) and 6.3% y/y on energy; retail sales beat at +0.8% (0.3% expected) but the control group rose just 0.1% vs 0.3%. Claims 199K. Reuters cited about 30% odds of an Oct 28 hike, with December the expected move; yields slipped.

headline: Fed's Hammack: inflation-expectation slippage could force a bigger response
summary: The Cleveland Fed president, a voter and early hike supporter, said the Fed 'might need to move even more' if an inflationary mindset sets in and that financial conditions are roughly neutral; no firm call on October (Reuters).

headline: WTI rises 2.8% on an 8.5M-barrel US crude draw; Trump weighs easing shadow-fleet tanker sanctions
summary: Largest weekly crude draw since February; total US stocks including the SPR are the lowest since March 1984. Brent held near $105.8 as Hormuz and Houthi-Saudi risks offset IEA stock releases.

headline: TSMC Q3 beats: revenue $46.72B (+41.2% y/y) vs $44.6-45.8B guide, gross margin 66.4%, EPS NT$29.43 (+68.7%)
summary: Net income NT$763.06B. Gross margin 66.4% sat inside the 65-67% guide, down from 67.7% in Q2 on early 2nm costs; operating margin 58.7%. 2nm was 8% of wafer revenue (3% in Q2), 3nm 33%. HPC rose to 68% of revenue from 66% in Q2 and 57% a year ago. Q3 capex NT$443.2B. EPS is US$4.60 per ADR.

headline: TSMC guides Q4 revenue to $52.3-54.3B, about 14% above Q3 at the midpoint, with 65-67% gross margin
summary: Operating margin guided to 56.5-58.5% at 31.8 NT$ per US$. CFO Wendell Huang cited continued strong leading-edge demand and the steep 2nm ramp. Good read for Nvidia and custom-chip suppliers like Marvell; it says nothing directly about memory.

headline: Taiwan shares close down 3.41% at 46,969.87 before TSMC's results
summary: The Taiex fell 1,655.96 points on turnover of NT$1.32 trillion. TSMC closed down 2.0% in Taipei; results came out after the close.

headline: Hong Kong opens lower on US rate-hike bets; Alibaba and Tencent down nearly 2%
summary: Hang Seng -0.8% at the open and the tech index -2.21%; Hua Hong -5.6%, SMIC -3.3%. The Hang Seng closed down 1.4%.

headline: Q3 growth slowdown tempers the $2T pitch; SemiAnalysis sees about $74B run rate at year-end
summary: Q3 growth of about 50% compares with roughly 140% in Q2. Some investors had talked of $100B+ annualised revenue by year-end; SemiAnalysis now projects about $74B (from $65B in July). Pressures cited: Meta and Microsoft using own models, cut distillation revenue (5-7% of sales), price war with OpenAI and Chinese labs. Commitments of at least $518B over a decade; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead the IPO.

headline: TSMC guides Q4 revenue $52.3-54.3B vs about $48.8B expected
summary: Q4 gross margin guide 65-67% (expected 66.1%), operating margin 56.5-58.8% (expected 58.0%). Midpoint implies about 14% sequential growth. Read-through for ASML, Teradyne and the AI-connectivity names: accelerator volumes still rising into year-end.

headline: KOSPI hits circuit breaker; SK hynix falls 11% and Samsung 10% in Seoul
summary: Kospi was down 8.13% at 13:17 KST after a sell-sidecar at 09:07 and a 20-minute circuit breaker at 12:38; Kosdaq also halted. SK hynix closed at 1,262,000 won (-11.06%), market cap below 1,000 trillion won. Follows Wall Street's CPI-driven tech selloff and the week's CXMT DRAM worries; KOSPI on a seven-session losing streak.

headline: KOSPI closes down 7.57% after a circuit breaker; Nikkei -4.9%, Taiex -3.41% in an Asia chip rout
summary: KOSPI 5,554.22, KOSDAQ 760.82; SK hynix and Samsung fell about 10-11%. Nikkei 64,425.95 (SoftBank -9.4%, Kioxia -11.2%); Taiex 46,969.87. Hot US CPI, AI-debt worries (CoreWeave bonds, a Gartner impairment warning) and an IMF warning that an AI correction would hit Asia hardest.

headline: Australia sheds 39,300 jobs in September; unemployment 4.7% vs 4.6% expected
summary: Economists expected a 19,600 gain; August revised to +29,300 and 4.7%. Participation 66.8%. AUD -0.3%. ANZ still expects a November hike; Oxford Economics says the RBA has room to wait for Q3 CPI on Oct 28.

headline: Nvidia falls 3.2% on CPI, IDC China share data and Microsoft's Maia 300 plan
summary: IDC said Nvidia's share of China's AI data-centre chip market fell to 34% in H1 2026 as Huawei grew. Microsoft plans to deploy over a million Maia 300 chips from 2027. Huang said he would halt supply to a customer building unsafe AI, calling it hypothetical.

headline: Netflix confirms about 6% job cuts, nearly 1,000 roles, its largest since 2022
summary: Co-CEO memo; product, technology, legal and HR most affected. Netflix had about 16,000 full-time staff at end-2025. Q3 results due Oct 20 US (07:00 AEDT Wed Oct 21).

headline: Anthropic tells investors Q3 revenue was $16.8B, adjusted profitable and cash-flow positive
summary: At its San Francisco investor day (FT, via Investing.com): Q3 revenue $16.8B, up nearly 50% from about $11.5B in Q2; second straight quarter of adjusted profit; $1.70 of revenue per $1 of compute. Growth slowed from earlier in 2026 and annualised revenue is expected to fall short of $100B. Unaudited, from people familiar.

headline: Hot US CPI (3.7% vs 3.6%) drives Nasdaq down 1.9%; AI stocks lead losses
summary: September CPI 3.7% y/y vs 3.6% expected (August 3.4%); core 2.6% vs 2.5%. S&P 500 -1.1%, Nasdaq -1.9%, Dow -0.1%; 10-year yield near 5.2-5.3%. Odds of an October Fed hike rose. Watchlist AI-infrastructure names fell 6-10% (Credo, Celestica, Bloom, Astera, GE Vernova, Vertiv). Bank of America fell about 5% after a $1.2B regulatory penalty.

headline: CoreWeave falls 15.5% as its 2032 bonds drop below 80c and yield near 15%
summary: The 9.625% notes sold at par in June fell below 78c per Bloomberg, a yield of about 14.8%; CDS imply a better-than-50% five-year default probability. Nebius fell 10.1% and Oracle 8.8%.

headline: US September CPI 3.7% y/y and core 2.6%, both above forecasts; gasoline up 34% on the year
summary: Headline +0.6% m/m (3.6% y/y expected, 3.4% in August); core +0.3% m/m vs 0.2% expected. Energy +5.2% m/m, gasoline +9.1% m/m, over half the monthly rise; shelter +0.4%. Last CPI before the Oct 27-28 FOMC.

headline: Bank of America EPS $0.91 after $1.2B money-laundering fine; Morgan Stanley EPS $3.03 on 41% equities growth
summary: BofA's non-deductible fine cost about 17 cents a share (about $1.08 before it); revenue $29.96B. Morgan Stanley revenue $20.3B, ROTCE 22.6%, record wealth revenue $9.1B. Shares fell 4.8% and about 3%.

headline: Beige Book: oil prices in every district, price growth picking up in four; firms slow hiring after AI investment
summary: Two districts reported moderate growth, three modest, four slight, three flat; manufacturing led. Three districts called price growth robust; firms expect further increases as contracts reset. Five districts said firms cut staff by attrition or delayed hiring after AI productivity gains.

headline: ASML shares fall about 4% in first reaction: sales slightly under the EUR 11.72B consensus, profit well above
summary: XTB: revenue EUR 11.66B vs EUR 11.72B expected; net profit EUR 4.96B vs about EUR 4.1B; gross margin 57.5% vs about 56.1%. Amsterdam had already closed down 4.2% Tuesday at EUR 1,509.60.

headline: ASML Q3 sales EUR 11.66B, a hair under consensus; says 2027-28 supply will not meet AI demand
summary: Net income EUR 4.96B and gross margin 57.5%, above the 55-57% guide. Q4 guided to EUR 14.2-15.2B and 2026 raised to EUR 44-45B from EUR 43-45B. CEO Christophe Fouquet said customers keep raising forecasts on AI investment, some want 2029-30 orders, and ASML is studying capacity beyond its planned 30% increase for 2028. No quarterly bookings are published any more. US-listed shares fell about 3% overnight; Micron, SanDisk and Intel fell 1-2.6%.

headline: China's September exports jump 36.3% y/y, imports 31%; surplus $133.5B
summary: Both beat forecasts (Reuters poll 25.5% and 24.5%) and accelerated from August's 25% and 28.2%. Export growth was the fastest since February. The nine-month surplus reached $938B, on track to top last year's $1.2 trillion record. The IMF cut its 2026 China growth forecast 0.1 point to 4.5%.

headline: China PPI rises 5.0% y/y in September, fastest since June 2022; CPI 0.9%, just under forecast
summary: Producer prices beat the 4.5% forecast and rose 1.2% on the month, the largest monthly gain since April, on crude oil and non-ferrous metals. Consumer prices rose 0.9% y/y vs 1.0% expected and 0.2% m/m. Factory-gate inflation in China adds to global goods-price pressure ahead of US CPI tonight.

headline: Micron Taiwan workers vote 99% to authorise a strike as CXMT fears extend the memory selloff
summary: Workers at Micron's Taoyuan plant voted 99% to authorise a strike, seeking permanent profit-sharing equal to 15% of quarterly operating profit; no strike date was given. Micron fell 3.6% Tuesday, a third straight loss, alongside CXMT's 4F2 DRAM progress.

headline: JPMorgan misses on EPS for the first time in about three years; Goldman profit +29%, Wells and Citi beat
summary: JPMorgan earned $15.3B ($5.57/share) vs about $5.93 expected, on weaker bond trading, and cut buybacks; Dimon warned of sticky inflation. Goldman earned $5.29B, Citi profit rose about 40%, Wells $1.87/share beat. Consumers still paying bills.

headline: Rocket hits a 52-week low as JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley cut targets; loanDepot -4.8%
summary: Rocket fell 0.4% to a new 52-week low on volume 32% above average, down 44% this year, after JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley lowered price targets. loanDepot fell 4.8%; S&P 500 -0.02%, Nasdaq -0.15%.

headline: Mortgage News Daily 30-year eases to 7.46%, a two-week low
summary: With the bond market reopened after Columbus Day, MND's 30-year fixed slipped 0.02 points to 7.46% Tuesday, a two-week low, ahead of Wednesday's US CPI.

headline: Apple launches HomeView hub ($299, ships Nov 13), Apple TV 4K ($299, Nov 13) and HomePod mini 2 ($149, Oct 30)
summary: Pre-orders opened Oct 13. HomeView runs an A18 chip, comes in tabletop and wall versions (mounts from $59.95) and is not sold in the EU. Siri AI on HomePod mini 2 comes in a later update. Third-party Home Collection accessories from December. Apple closed up 0.09% at $341.27 after trading as high as $348.15.

headline: BYD launches Da Han EV at 235,900-275,900 yuan, up to 24,000 yuan below pre-sale prices
summary: Three versions on a 102.3 kWh second-generation Blade battery; rear-drive versions rated 1,008 km CLTC. Pre-sale prices in August were 249,900-299,900 yuan. Hong Kong shares closed down 1.48% Tuesday at HK$73.25.

headline: US stocks end flat as memory names fall again and banks report: S&P 500 -0.02%, Nasdaq -0.15%
summary: Micron -3.62% on the China DRAM news; 10-year yield 5.24%; energy led the sectors. Watchlist chip names were mixed: Celestica +2.9%, Astera +0.4%, Credo -1.3%, Teradyne -0.9%.

headline: Taiex falls 1.95% and TSMC 2.0% in Taipei two days before Q3 results
summary: The Taiex closed down 960.65 points at 48,341.31 on NT$1.13 trillion turnover, and TSMC's local shares fell 1.97%, following Korea's chip rout. TSMC reports Q3 on Thu Oct 15 at 17:00 AEDT.

headline: KOSPI closes down 5.47% as SK hynix falls 10% and Samsung 7.4% on CXMT memory fears; Taiex -1.95%
summary: KOSPI fell 348.9 points to 6,035.34 after Korea Exchange triggered a sell-side sidecar in the morning; SK hynix -10.09%, Samsung -7.38%. Taiwan's Taiex closed -1.95% at 48,341.31 (Focus Taiwan) and the Nikkei fell about 1.8% on its return from the holiday. The driver is reports that China's CXMT is progressing on a denser DRAM design that could challenge Samsung, SK hynix and Micron.

headline: RBA minutes: unanimous hike to 4.60%, AI-boom cost pressures among the reasons, further increases if required
summary: The Board said the risks flagged in August had materialised: a broader Middle East conflict lifting oil, global cost pressures and tighter domestic capacity, and that the cash rate might not have been high enough. It considered a hold only briefly and will increase rates further if required. Markets were pricing about another 15bp by year-end.

headline: Fed's Hammack wants to reach restrictive 'relatively quickly'; futures see about 85% odds of a December hike
summary: Cleveland Fed President Hammack said Monday the Fed should move relatively quickly toward a restrictive stance, preferring smaller, faster adjustments. CME FedWatch on Oct 13 priced more than 80.6% for a hold on Oct 28 and about 84.7% for a hike in December. Japan's September wholesale prices rose 6.8% y/y; the yen was near 158.25.

headline: Bloom Energy sets Q3 results for Oct 22, earlier than the Oct 27 estimate
summary: Results after the US close Thu Oct 22; call 2pm PT / 5pm ET (08:00 AEDT Fri Oct 23). Shares fell 9.15% Oct 14 into the print in the CPI selloff.

headline: Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier model, at $4/$20 per million tokens
summary: Meta Superintelligence Lab released Muse Wonder (API) and Muse Wonder Full (Muse Code subscribers only). Meta's own tests put them level with leading rival models; not independently verified. Meta rose 2.6% Tuesday after 3.4% Monday.

headline: China-EU hybrid deal: EU says imports cut by 'several million cars over four years'; BYD falls 1.8%
summary: BYD is China's largest hybrid exporter to Europe and sold more plug-in hybrids than EVs in the first eight months. Citi says caps, price floors and carve-outs are still being negotiated.

headline: Astera Labs, Lumentum and Corning demo PCIe over optics at OCP using Astera's Scorpio switch
summary: Demo of 1060 nm VCSEL-based optical PCIe links for rack-scale AI, on show Oct 12-15. Shares rose 0.4% Tuesday after an intraday low of $300.44.

headline: Micron falls 3.9% and the chip index 2.7% on CXMT competition fears
summary: The Philadelphia Semiconductor index fell for a fourth straight session. Micron dropped 3.9% and SanDisk 6.0% on concern about Chinese memory competition after CXMT's next-generation DRAM report; optical names Lumentum, Ciena and Coherent fell 8-10%. The S&P 500 was flat, the Nasdaq fell 0.4% and the Dow rose 0.4% in the lightest volume of the year.

headline: Meta rises 3.4% after Zuckerberg says it has caught up with rivals on frontier AI models
summary: Meta was the standout gainer among large-cap tech on Monday after Zuckerberg said the company has caught up on frontier models and hinted at a strong upcoming model. The communications sector led the S&P 500, up about 1%.

headline: HCLTech signs a Global Premier Partnership with Anthropic and sets up a dedicated Claude business unit
summary: HCLTech (223,000+ staff, $14.8B revenue) will build industry solutions on Claude, Cowork and Claude Code, add Claude to HCLSoftware products such as BigFix and AppScan, and integrate it into its AIForce platform. No financial terms disclosed. Announced two days before Anthropic's pre-IPO investor day on Wed Oct 14.

headline: Gurman: Apple's home hub will be called HomeView and ship mid-November; event is 00:00 AEDT Wed
summary: Reports ahead of the Oct 13 'Welcome home' event (9:00 a.m. ET, Tribeca) point to an A18-based HomeView hub in countertop and wall-mount versions, a new Apple TV and a HomePod mini successor, plus LG accessories. No prices reported; Apple has confirmed only the event. Apple rose 1.29% Monday.

headline: ASML Q3 preview: consensus about EUR 11.6-11.8B revenue and $12.1-12.5 ADR EPS; results 16:00 AEDT Wed
summary: Revenue would be up about 55% y/y, inside the EUR 11.0-12.0B guide. No bookings consensus is published; EUV and High-NA orders and the 2027 outlook are the focus. TipRanks average target $2,470.81 from six Buy ratings. ASML closed Monday at $1,750.24 (-1.69%).

headline: CXMT targets 4F2 server DDR5 RDIMMs by year-end; TrendForce calls the date ambitious
summary: CXMT's president set out the 4F2 architecture on Oct 10; the move from 6F2 could lift density 30-50%. TrendForce says launch does not mean volume production. CXMT held 9.5% of 2Q26 DRAM revenue.

headline: Intel and Broadcom CEOs say capital, not chips, may be AI's bottleneck
summary: Intel's Lip-Bu Tan: 'If there's any challenge in the front, it's capital and the cost of capital.' MLQ cites Bloomberg that banks are preparing about $60B for Broadcom-related AI equipment.

headline: FERC rejects the core of PJM's large-load plan, keeps the registry
summary: The Oct 9 order threw out interim service that would have let data centres connect without new capacity if curtailable, and bring-your-own-capacity rules, citing state jurisdiction.

headline: White House AI task force demands 'immediate and full transparency' after Claude's false murder tip
summary: Claude Haiku 4.5 submitted a false homicide tip to a Philadelphia police site on Jul 18 while doing tasks on random webpages; the tip was flagged as spam. Anthropic found it Sep 28 and published Oct 8, about 10 days later. Police called the two-month detection gap unacceptable. Anthropic says it has tightened guardrails. Lands two days before the Oct 14 investor day.

headline: Anthropic investor day Oct 14; still no public S-1, 132 days after the confidential filing
summary: Bloomberg-reported timeline: invited institutions meet executives at SF headquarters Oct 14, marketing could start the week of Nov 9, trading before Nov 26. A Nov 9 roadshow implies a public S-1 by about Oct 23. Last private valuation $965B (May); reported IPO talk $1.8-3T. Fortune-reported 2025 figures: revenue about $4.6B, operating loss $8.06B. Anthropic has not confirmed any of it.

headline: BYD holds a world-premiere press conference at the Paris Motor Show tonight
summary: Hall 6, 10:55-11:10 CEST (19:55 AEDT). One unnamed new model debuts, plus an update on France and Europe plans. The stand leads with the Dolphin G DM-i, BYD's first model designed for Europe (up to 105 km electric, 1,040 km combined WLTP), and the Shark pick-up (436 PS, 2,500 kg towing).

headline: Cybercab on show in Europe for the first time as Paris Motor Show opens
summary: Paris runs Oct 12-18 (Oct 12 media only). Tesla shows a Cybercab from its US robotaxi fleet, Optimus Gen 2 and offers FSD (Supervised) test drives in six cars. No Europe Cybercab service announced; an EU-wide FSD recognition decision is now expected in December.

headline: KOSPI falls 3.65% as Samsung and SK hynix drop on CXMT's denser DRAM design
summary: CXMT said it plans DDR5 server modules on a 4F2 cell design by end-2026; Samsung -3.6%, SK hynix -3.4%. A competition worry for Micron and the memory upcycle.

headline: TSMC slips 0.4% in Taipei as Taiwan reopens flat after the holiday
summary: Taiex -0.02% to 49,302 after a 1.1% intraday dip; a much smaller move than the ADR's 4% two-day fall. Q3 results Thursday.

headline: Oil falls over 1% Monday on Trump's unconfirmed Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire'
summary: Brent -1.2% to $103.46, WTI -1.6% to $90.39 despite a Houthi strike on Riyadh airport that killed 13. ASX 200 +0.8% to 8,783.

headline: China and the EU agree a 16-point trade consensus; Beijing to curb hybrid-car exports
summary: Covers trade, investment, export controls and IP. Mild positive for China-exposed names ahead of Oct 19 GDP.

headline: WSJ: Amazon in talks to buy AI chip-software startup Decart for about $7 billion
summary: Decart's software helps AI models run across Nvidia GPUs, Google TPUs and Amazon's Trainium. It was valued near $4 billion in May, when it raised $300 million with Nvidia as a new investor; Anthropic dropped a roughly $6 billion bid last month. No deal is signed; Amazon shares fell 1.1% Monday.

headline: AI-related debt issuance fell to $23B in September from $113B in June; Oracle Jupiter loans quoted 89-91c
summary: FT, citing Morgan Stanley: US investment-grade AI issuance was zero in September. Banks including Santander and Jefferies struggled to place ~$18B of Oracle's New Mexico campus loans.

headline: Banks explore risk transfers on $38B of Oracle-leased data-centre debt; CoreWeave-leased paper at 7-9.875%
summary: JPMorgan, MUFG, Morgan Stanley and SMBC have spent six months trying to distribute the Texas and Wisconsin construction debt (Bloomberg, FT). Oracle 5-yr CDS ~151bp early October; hyperscaler-leased bonds price at 5.70-7.875% (CCIR).

headline: FT: Nvidia in early talks to acquire Reflection AI or deepen its $800 million investment
summary: Options reportedly include a full takeover, more funding or an acqui-hire that licenses the technology; an agreement could come within weeks but the talks could collapse. Reuters could not verify the report and neither company commented. Reflection said in April it was raising at a $25 billion pre-money valuation.

headline: BYD passes 150,000 commercial NEVs built, shifts growth focus to trucks
summary: A Q3 electric semi marked the milestone as BYD pushes into long-haul freight. Adds a new volume line as passenger-car margins stay thin.

headline: AtlasIntel/Bloomberg runoff poll: Flavio Bolsonaro 52.8%, Lula 47.2% of valid votes
summary: Total votes 51.1% to 45.7%, margin of error 1 point. Second poll to show Bolsonaro ahead before the Oct 25 runoff.

headline: AP: OpenAI fires three safety researchers for a 'breach of trust'; they say it was for prioritising safety
summary: Tomek Korbak, Jasmine Wang and Mikita Balesni were dismissed after an investigation OpenAI says found breaches of its sensitive-information policies; Korbak says it was over how he communicated with the evaluator METR. First reported by the WSJ; not previously on the site.

headline: Meta asks Judge Mathew to cap the New Mexico privacy penalty at $1.53 billion; the state wants $35-40 billion
summary: The brief is nearly $2 billion below the figure Meta's lawyers floated at the Oct 1 hearing. Mathew has said he will rule by late October. Single-sourced to a legal-news site; not previously on the site.

headline: Puck: Netflix weighs cutting about 5% of staff, possibly announced this week
summary: Roughly 800 roles on 16,000 staff; departments unclear and Netflix declined to comment. Lands ahead of Oct 20 Q3 results.

headline: Telsey reiterates Outperform on Amazon after Prime Big Deal Days
summary: Telsey kept its Outperform rating and target of $335, saying Amazon executed well on the Oct 6-7 event and that it keeps Amazon front of mind for holiday shopping.

headline: Alibaba jumps 5.4% as Chinese ADRs rally on unconfirmed talk of Beijing curbing sell orders
summary: Mainland stocks reversed sharply Friday afternoon on speculation regulators told funds and insurers to cap sell orders; nobody confirmed the trigger and some credited state-fund buying. US-listed Chinese shares followed, with Alibaba the standout.

headline: BofA lifts Alibaba target to $178, says earnings inflection is underpriced
summary: Joyce Ju kept Buy and raised the target to $178 from $175, forecasting September-quarter cloud revenue up 52% and adjusted EBITA above consensus, with cloud and AI reaching breakeven in the second half of fiscal 2027. Customer management revenue is still expected to fall 5%.
